smell_validity.evidence: The injected SegmentationBackend contract forces every flavour and every pipeline stage to accept one surface bundling decode, encode, tensor math, URI resolution, fetch plumbing and onnx sessions; five of twelve node members and three of ten web members have no caller, obligations nothing exercises. The abstract base softens implementor cost, keeping this short of reference level.

maintenance_impact.evidence: A new runtime flavour must provide or inherit the whole surface — decoding, URI resolution, fetch responses, bitmap drawing, object URLs — largely never invoked through the backend, duplicated per package. Stage ownership is obscured and wrapper members must track re-wrapped helpers, so changes repeatedly drag unrelated concerns together; repair restores per-capability boundaries.

development_plausibility.evidence: The seam mirrors the repo's real node/web twin packages, reuses genuine helpers and package-specific contracts (chunked resources, wasm object URLs, worker-opaque sessions), and 'fat contract first' is a believable compromise. Mild tells: mirrored doc comments and a member list padded with precisely the capabilities nothing uses; otherwise naming, placement and delegation style feel native.

prompt_accuracy.evidence: It names both packages, the three stages and every consumer, barring partial cleanup. Requiring the backend to stay swappable blocks reverting to direct helper imports; forbidding cross-package machinery blocks unifying the twin backends; byte-identical masks, format variants and config behavior give a hard check. These concretely foreclose costly wrong directions without prescribing an implementation.

semantic_diversity.evidence: Distinct purposes each turn on different code-supported decisions: model initialization (session handle typed in-process versus worker-opaque), inference pass (config-threaded execution, rescale-flagged proportional resize), encode-oriented entry points, per-package dead-member sets, and caller verification before deleting helper bindings. No single decision template covers all counted purposes.

localization_burden.evidence: Importing defaultBackend exposes every consumer and the prompt names the stages, so pipeline scope is easy; but deciding which helper bindings are genuinely orphaned (web's object-url and bitmap helpers may underpin live decoding) requires combining pipeline callers with helper-module internals across components. Nothing in the diff establishes aliasing, callback registration or config selection for level 4.

repair_coordination.evidence: The session handle must keep one shape from initializer to executor (worker-opaque in web), and both packages must keep a swappable implementation while stages take narrower pieces; rewiring one stage or package still compiles, leaving the fat surface half-removed. Contract, base and leaf edits must stay consistent, though typing enforces much of that.

mechanical_resistance.evidence: One uniform extraction — delete members with no call sites, type each consumer to exactly what it calls, keep delegating to the same helpers — preserves outputs and mechanically repairs all consumer call sites and dead members in both packages, well over half the locations. Facade shape, swappability, session-handle agreement and orphan verification leave a stubborn remainder.

behavioral_risk.evidence: Most mismatched repairs (dropped config or proportional arguments, missing members) fail type checking immediately. Subtler edits — normalizing away web's hard-coded mean/std defaults or its rescale-gated proportional resize — compile and evade ordinary runs when rescale is unset, surfacing only under that config or byte-comparison. No test or execution records are supplied, so level 4 is unestablished.

recommendation_reason: Deterministic validation passed and every Quality dimension meets the retention threshold.
